1.34.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/alloc/slice.rs.html#312-315)#### pub fn [sort_by_cached_key](https://docs.rs#method.sort_by_cached_key)<K, F>(&mut self, f: F)

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/alloc/slice.rs.html#312-315)

#### pub fn [sort_by_cached_key](https://docs.rs#method.sort_by_cached_key)<K, F>(&mut self, f: F)

Sorts the slice in ascending order with a key extraction function, preserving initial order of equal elements.

This sort is stable (i.e., does not reorder equal elements) and *O*(*m* * *n* + *n* *
log(*n*)) worst-case, where the key function is *O*(*m*).

During sorting, the key function is called at most once per element, by using temporary storage to remember the results of key evaluation. The order of calls to the key function is unspecified and may change in future versions of the standard library.

If the implementation of [ Ord](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/trait.Ord.html) for

`K` does not implement a [total order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_order), the function may panic; even if the function exits normally, the resulting order of elements in the slice is unspecified. See also the note on panicking below.

For simple key functions (e.g., functions that are property accesses or basic operations),
[ sort_by_key](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.sort_by_key) is likely to be faster.

[§](https://docs.rs#current-implementation-9)Current implementation

The current implementation is based on [instruction-parallel-network sort](https://github.com/Voultapher/sort-research-rs/tree/main/ipnsort) by Lukas
Bergdoll, which combines the fast average case of randomized quicksort with the fast worst
case of heapsort, while achieving linear time on fully sorted and reversed inputs. And
*O*(*k* * log(*n*)) where *k* is the number of distinct elements in the input. It leverages
superscalar out-of-order execution capabilities commonly found in CPUs, to efficiently
perform the operation.

In the worst case, the algorithm allocates temporary storage in a `Vec<(K, usize)>` the
length of the slice.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-56)Panics

May panic if the implementation of [ Ord](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/trait.Ord.html) for

`K` does not implement a [total order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_order), or if the

[implementation panics.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/trait.Ord.html)

`Ord`All safe functions on slices preserve the invariant that even if the function panics, all
original elements will remain in the slice and any possible modifications via interior
mutability are observed in the input. This ensures that recovery code (for instance inside
of a `Drop` or following a `catch_unwind`) will still have access to all the original
elements. For instance, if the slice belongs to a `Vec`, the `Vec::drop` method will be able
to dispose of all contained elements.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-163)Examples

```
let mut v = [4i32, -5, 1, -3, 2, 10];
// Strings are sorted by lexicographical order.
v.sort_by_cached_key(|k| k.to_string());
assert_eq!(v, [-3, -5, 1, 10, 2, 4]);
```

Check if this key has been “read”, i.e. it exists in the memory overlay.

Can be true if the key has been read, has been written to, or has been whitelisted.

Can be true if the key has been written to, or has been whitelisted.

# ChildType in sp_storage - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sp-storage/^25.0.0/enum.ChildType.html

```
#[repr(u32)]pub enum ChildType {
    ParentKeyId = 1,
}
```
## Expand description

Type of child. It does not strictly define different child type, it can also be related to technical consideration or api variant.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ParentKeyId)

### ParentKeyId = 1

If runtime module ensures that the child key is a unique id that will only be used once, its parent key is used as a child trie unique id.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

# StateVersion in sp_storage - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sp-storage/^25.0.0/enum.StateVersion.html

```
pub enum StateVersion {
    V0 = 0,
    V1 = 1,
}
```
## Expand description

Different possible state version.

V0 and V1 uses a same trie implementation, but V1 will write external value node in the trie for
value with size at least `TRIE_VALUE_NODE_THRESHOLD`.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-StateVersion)

### impl [StateVersion](https://docs.rs/enum.StateVersion.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sp_storage/lib.rs.html#472-477)#### pub fn [state_value_threshold](https://docs.rs#method.state_value_threshold)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sp_storage/lib.rs.html#472-477)

#### pub fn [state_value_threshold](https://docs.rs#method.state_value_threshold)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)>

If defined, values in state of size bigger or equal to this threshold will use a separate trie node. Otherwise, value will be inlined in branch or leaf node.

# sp_externalities - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/sp-externalities/latest/target-redirect/sp_externalities/index.html

## Expand description

Substrate externalities abstraction

The externalities mainly provide access to storage and to registered extensions. Extensions are for example the keystore or the offchain externalities. These externalities are used to access the node from the runtime via the runtime interfaces.

This crate exposes the main [ Externalities](https://docs.rs/trait.Externalities.html) trait.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [decl_](https://docs.rs/macro.decl_extension.html)- extension
- Macro for declaring an extension that usable with `Extensions`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Extensions](https://docs.rs/struct.Extensions.html)
- Stores extensions that should be made available through the externalities.
- [Multi](https://docs.rs/struct.MultiRemovalResults.html)- Removal - Results
- Results concerning an operation to remove many keys.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- Externalities error.
- [Transaction](https://docs.rs/enum.TransactionType.html)- Type
- Informs `Extension`

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Extension](https://docs.rs/trait.Extension.html)
- Marker trait for types that should be registered as `Externalities`
- [Extension](https://docs.rs/trait.ExtensionStore.html)- Store
- Something that provides access to the `Extensions`
- [Externalities](https://docs.rs/trait.Externalities.html)
- The Substrate externalities.
- [Externalities](https://docs.rs/trait.ExternalitiesExt.html)- Ext
- Extension for the `Externalities`

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [set_](https://docs.rs/fn.set_and_run_with_externalities.html)- and_ - run_ - with_ - externalities
- Set the given externalities while executing the given closure. To get access to the
externalities while executing the given closure `with_externalities`
- [with_](https://docs.rs/fn.with_externalities.html)- externalities
- Execute the given closure with the currently set externalities.

}## Expand description

The Substrate externalities.

Provides access to the storage and to other registered extensions.

#### fn [kill_child_storage](https://docs.rs#tymethod.kill_child_storage)(
    &mut self,
    child_info: &[ChildInfo](https://docs.rs/sp-storage/25.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sp_storage/enum.ChildInfo.html),
    maybe_limit: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)>,
    maybe_cursor: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)]>,
) -> [MultiRemovalResults](https://docs.rs/struct.MultiRemovalResults.html)

Clear an entire child storage.

Deletes all keys from the overlay and up to `maybe_limit` keys from the backend. No
limit is applied if `maybe_limit` is `None`. Returns the cursor for the next call as `Some`
if the child trie deletion operation is incomplete. In this case, it should be passed into
the next call to avoid unaccounted iterations on the backend. Returns also the the number
of keys that were removed from the backend, the number of unique keys removed in total
(including from the overlay) and the number of backend iterations done.

As long as `maybe_cursor` is passed from the result of the previous call, then the number of
iterations done will only ever be one more than the number of keys removed.

[§](https://docs.rs#note)Note

An implementation is free to delete more keys than the specified limit as long as it is able to do that in constant time.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sp_externalities/lib.rs.html#227)#### fn [storage_start_transaction](https://docs.rs#tymethod.storage_start_transaction)(&mut self)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sp_externalities/lib.rs.html#227)

#### fn [storage_start_transaction](https://docs.rs#tymethod.storage_start_transaction)(&mut self)

Start a new nested transaction.

This allows to either commit or roll back all changes made after this call to the
top changes or the default child changes. For every transaction there cam be a
matching call to either `storage_rollback_transaction` or `storage_commit_transaction`.
Any transactions that are still open after returning from runtime are committed
automatically.

Changes made without any open transaction are committed immediately.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sp_externalities/lib.rs.html#233)#### fn [storage_rollback_transaction](https://docs.rs#tymethod.storage_rollback_transaction)(&mut self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sp_externalities/lib.rs.html#233)

Rollback the last transaction started by `storage_start_transaction`.

# decl_extension in sp_externalities - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/sp-externalities/latest/target-redirect/sp_externalities/macro.decl_extension.html

```
macro_rules! decl_extension {
    (
		$( #[ $attr:meta ] )*
		$vis:vis struct $ext_name:ident ($inner:ty);
		$(
			impl $ext_name_impl:ident {
				$(
					$impls:tt
				)*
			}
		)*
	) => { ... };
    (
		$( #[ $attr:meta ] )*
		$vis:vis struct $ext_name:ident;
	) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Macro for declaring an extension that usable with [ Extensions](https://docs.rs/struct.Extensions.html).

The extension will be an unit wrapper struct that implements [ Extension](https://docs.rs/trait.Extension.html),

`Deref` and
`DerefMut`. The wrapped type is given by the user.[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
decl_extension! {
    /// Some test extension
    struct TestExt(String);
}
```
The [ Extension](https://docs.rs/trait.Extension.html) trait provides hooks that are called when starting, committing or rolling back
a transaction. These can be implemented with the macro as well:

```
decl_extension! {
    /// Some test extension
    struct TestExtWithCallback(String);
    impl TestExtWithCallback {
        fn start_transaction(&mut self, ty: TransactionType) {
            // do something cool
        }
        // The other methods `commit_transaction` and `rollback_transaction` can also
        // be implemented in the same way.
    }
}
```

`maybe_cursor: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>>A continuation cursor which, if `Some` must be provided to the subsequent removal call.
If `None` then all removals are complete and no further calls are needed.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.backend)

`backend: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)The number of items removed from the backend database.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.unique)

`unique: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)The number of unique keys removed, taking into account both the backend and the overlay.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.loops)

`loops: `[u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)The number of iterations (each requiring a storage seek/read) which were done.

`pub trait Extension: `[Send](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html) + 'static {
    // Required methods
    fn [as_mut_any](https://docs.rs#tymethod.as_mut_any)(&mut self) -> &mut dyn [Any](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/any/trait.Any.html);
[type_id](https://docs.rs#tymethod.type_id)(&self) -> [TypeId](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/any/struct.TypeId.html);
    // Provided methods

}## Expand description

Marker trait for types that should be registered as [ Externalities](https://docs.rs/trait.Externalities.html)
extension.

As extensions are stored as `Box<Any>`, this trait should give more confidence that the correct
type is registered and requested.
